      "body": "There is no uniqueness validation or database constraint for host, so Add Host can save the same hostname multiple times with different categories, including differently cased spellings. record_for_host returns only the first matching record, meaning a successfully saved or edited mapping on another row is silently ignored when topics are imported. findings.title: Handle missing category rows before indexing the query result
findings.body: When embed_category is unset, empty, or names a deleted category, the join returns no rows. Accessing [0]['id'] then raises before the uncategorized fallback can run. This blocks db:migrate for installations that never configured embedding, including clean installs. Read the result conditionally; the fallback query also needs to handle an absent persisted uncategorized_category_id setting.

findings.title: Normalize legacy host entries before inserting them
findings.body: The old allowlist supported full URLs such as http://discourse.org and https://example.com/1234, but this migration copies them verbatim. Direct SQL bypasses EmbeddableHost's callback that strips schemes and paths, while the new lookup compares the stored value with the bare URI hostname. After upgrading, these previously working entries no longer authorize embedding or topic retrieval. Apply the same hostname normalization during migration.

findings.title: Match port-qualified hosts consistently
findings.body: The model accepts example.com:8080 and retains the port in the stored host, but URI('http://example.com:8080/page').host returns only example.com. This query therefore cannot find the saved record. Administrators can successfully configure a port-qualified host, yet embedding requests from it are rejected and its category mapping is never found. Normalize stored entries and lookup keys consistently.

findings.title: Allow valid top-level domains longer than five characters
findings.body: The [a-z]{2,5} suffix rejects valid domains such as example.museum and example.technology. Stripping the scheme and path does not change that restriction, so administrators cannot save these legitimate embedding hosts in the new editor. Host validation should not impose a five-character maximum on top-level domains.

findings.title: Enforce one category mapping per normalized hostname
findings.body: There is no uniqueness validation or database constraint for host, so Add Host can save the same hostname multiple times with different categories, including differently cased spellings. record_for_host returns only the first matching record, meaning a successfully saved or edited mapping on another row is silently ignored when topics are imported. Enforce case-insensitive uniqueness for the normalized hostname so category routing is unambiguous.
